title: Construction and Codification Act
section: Sec. 1.001 — Short title.
text:
Sec. 1.001 — Short title.
This act may be cited as the “Construction and Codification Act”, AND HERE’S THE NEW EDITS!!!!!!!!!!

History: Add. 2026 AS 1 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026) ;— Am. 2026 AS 17 (eff. Oct 1, 2026).

title: Construction and Codification Act
section: Sec. 1.002 — Resolutions; require for legislation providing for acts of state; process.
text:
Sec. 1.002 — Resolutions; require for legislation providing for acts of state; process.
All legislation providing for an act of state must be by resolution of substantially similar form to this act that is introduced by a member of the Council of State by motion during a session thereof, debated by a quorum of members, and adopted by majority vote or unanimous consent of those members, subject to applicable law. A resolution that is rejected by a quorum of members of the Council of State is null and void.

History: Add. 2026 AS 1 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Construction and Codification Act
section: Sec. 1.003 — Resolutions; form and manner; unique identifier; title; enacting clause; enabling clause.
text:
Sec. 1.003 — Resolutions; form and manner; unique identifier; title; enacting clause; enabling clause.
A resolution furnished under this act must contain, but is not limited to, the following:

(a) A unique identifier.


(b) A title expressing the object of and the changes proposed by the resolution.


(c) An enacting clause of the form “BE IT ENACTED BY THE CROWN-IN-COUNCIL:”.


(d) An enabling clause of the form “BY AND UNDER THE GREAT SEAL OF THE REALM, SO ENACTED THIS [DD] DAY OF [MM], [YYYY].”, such that the bracketed text is replaced, respectively, with the long-form day, month, and year of the date upon which the Crown-in-Council granted assent to the resolution.


History: Add. 2026 AS 1 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Construction and Codification Act
section: Sec. 1.004 — Resolutions; form and manner; require reprinting and marking of changes.
text:
Sec. 1.004 — Resolutions; form and manner; require reprinting and marking of changes.
A resolution furnished under this act for the purpose of amending any section or sections of a law must reprint the object section or sections at length, in which insertions must be marked by boldface text and deletions must be marked by strikethrough text.

History: Add. 2026 AS 1 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Construction and Codification Act
section: Sec. 1.006 — Eniarku Compiled Laws; require codification of Constitution and laws; “law” defined; order of codification; titles.
text:
Sec. 1.006 — Eniarku Compiled Laws; require codification of Constitution and laws; “law” defined; order of codification; titles.
(1) The Constitution and all laws shall be recorded in the Eniarku Compiled Laws. As used in this act, “law” means any of the following:

(a) An act of state.


(b) Orders-in-council.


(c) Letters patent.


(d) A sovereign proclamation.

(2) The Constitution shall be codified in the Eniarku Compiled Laws before Title 1.
(3) Acts of state shall be codified in the Eniarku Compiled Laws such that the first digit of a section identifier corresponds to one of the following titles:

(a) Title 1 – General Provisions


(b) Title 2 – The Public Welfare and Security


(c) Title 3 – The Crown and Royal House


(d) Title 4 – National Honours and Nobility


(e) Title 5 – The Council of State


(f) Title 6 – National Symbols


(g) Title 7 – The Realm


(h) Title 8 – Commerce and Trade


(i) Title 9 – Domestic Affairs


(j) Title 10 – Foreign Affairs

(4) Orders-in-council, letters patent, and sovereign proclamations shall be codified in the Eniarku Compiled Laws under the title that most closely corresponds to the subject matter of the instrument. Such instruments shall be codified in the Eniarku Compiled Laws using the unique identifier assigned to them by the issuing entity of the state.

History: Add. 2026 AS 1 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Construction and Codification Act
section: Sec. 1.007 — Eniarku Compiled Laws; repealed provisions; require printing with historical information.
text:
Sec. 1.007 — Eniarku Compiled Laws; repealed provisions; require printing with historical information.
Any provisions of the Eniarku Compiled Laws that is repealed by a resolution furnished under this act must be printed in the Eniarku Compiled Laws with sufficient historical information such that a reasonable person would be able to identify the previous versions of those provisions.



History: Add. 2026 AS 17 (eff. Oct 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
text:
Sec. 1.101 — Short title.
This act may be cited as the “Great Seal Act.

title: Great Seal Act
text: History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
section: Sec. 1.102 — Great seal; use as official seal.
text:
Sec. 1.102 — Great seal; use as official seal.
The Great Seal of the Realm shall be the official seal of The Sovereign and the state.

History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
section: Sec. 1.103 — Great seal; description.
text:
Sec. 1.103 — Great seal; description.
The Great Seal of the Realm shall be comprised of a lion, around which shall appear the words “MAGNUM SIGILLUM MAGNI DUCATUS”, around which shall appear the words “ALEXANDER PRIMUS PER GRATIAM ET VOLUNTATEM POPULI MAGNUS DUX REGNI DEFENSOR CONSTITUTIONIS ET CETERA”.

History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
section: Sec. 1.104 — Great seal; impression on certain documents.
text:
Sec. 1.104 — Great seal; impression on certain documents.
An electronic or material impression of the Great Seal of the Realm shall be placed on or affixed to those instruments which require the assent of The Sovereign to enter into effect. Any such instrument which does not bear the Great Seal of the Realm shall be considered null.

History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
section: Sec. 1.105 — Lord High Chancellor; establish; appointment and term of office.
text:
Sec. 1.105 — Lord High Chancellor; establish; appointment and term of office.
(1) The office of the Lord High Chancellor is established as an entity of the state.
(2) The Lord High Chancellor shall be appointed to his office and to the Council of State by, and serve at the pleasure of, The Sovereign.

History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
section: Sec. 1.106 — Great seal; prohibit use for unofficial purposes.
text:
Sec. 1.106 — Great seal; prohibit use for unofficial purposes.
No person or entity of the state, with the exception of the Lord High Chancellor or any other such person or entity of the state as provided by law, shall make or prepare any instrument bearing a facsimile or reproduction of the Great Seal of the Realm for any purposes unconnected with official functions of the state.

History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
section: Sec. 1.107 — Great seal; affixing to instruments by Lord High Chancellor.
text:
Sec. 1.107 — Great seal; affixing to instruments by Lord High Chancellor.
(1) Upon receipt of an adopted resolution of the Council of State providing for an act of state and a warrant issued by The Sovereign granting assent to that resolution, the Lord High Chancellor shall place on or affix to that resolution the Great Seal of the Realm.
(2) Upon receipt of orders-in-council, letters patent, or a sovereign proclamation issued by The Sovereign, the Lord High Chancellor shall place on or affix to that instrument the Great Seal of the Realm.

History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Great Seal Act
section: Sec. 1.108 – Great seal; violations as misdemeanor.
text:
Sec. 1.108 – Great seal; violations as misdemeanor.
A person who violates any provision of this act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.



History: Add. 2026 AS 2 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
text:
Sec. 5.001 — Short title.
This act may be cited as the “Internal Procedures Act.

title: Internal Procedures Act
text: History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
section: Sec. 5.002 — Regular sessions; member attendance.
text:
Sec. 5.002 — Regular sessions; member attendance.
The Council of State shall conduct all public business during regular sessions. Members shall attend sessions in person or by means of two-way video and audio technology.

History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
section: Sec. 5.003 — Quorum; require to conduct business.
text:
Sec. 5.003 — Quorum; require to conduct business.
The Council of State shall not conduct any public business unless a quorum of 51% or more of its members are present.

History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
section: Sec. 5.004 — Order of business.
text:
Sec. 5.004 — Order of business.
The Council of State shall conduct public business in the following sequence:

(a) Introductions of resolutions.


(b) Debates on resolutions, including, but not limited to, amendments and procedural motions.


(c) Votes on resolutions under consideration.


(d) Motions and procedural matters relating to the operations of the Council of State, including, but not limited to, the rules of the Council of State and scheduling matters.


(e) Any other public business.


History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
section: Sec. 5.005 — Crown-in-Council; equal vote.
text:
Sec. 5.005 — Crown-in-Council; equal vote.
A vote submitted by the Crown-in-Council during a session of the Council of State shall be considered equally to a vote submitted by any other member thereof.

History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
section: Sec. 5.006 — Internal rules; require two-thirds vote to adopt, amend, or repeal.
text:
Sec. 5.006 — Internal rules; require two-thirds vote to adopt, amend, or repeal.
The Council of State may, by a two-thirds vote of all members, adopt, amend, or repeal, in part or in entirety, certain rules governing the procedures and operations of the Council of State, including, but not limited to, those relating to the form and manner of debate and voting during a session thereof.

History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
section: Sec. 5.007 — Absence of rule governing certain conduct; applicability of generally acceptable parliamentary procedure; ruling of chair.
text:
Sec. 5.007 — Absence of rule governing certain conduct; applicability of generally acceptable parliamentary procedure; ruling of chair.
In the absence of a rule or procedure governing certain activities of the Council of State, the generally acceptable principles of parliamentary procedure shall apply, subject to a ruling of the member presently chairing the session to that effect.

History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).

title: Internal Procedures Act
section: Sec. 5.008 — Resolutions; effective date.
text:
Sec. 5.008 — Resolutions; effective date.
A resolution adopted by the Council of State and granted assent by The Sovereign that does not specify the effective date of the provisions thereof shall become effective at 12:00 AM on the day immediately following the date on which assent was granted.



History: Add. 2026 AS 3 (imd. eff. Jan 1, 2026).
